map.δ 随日期变化，春分/秋分约 0°，夏至约 +23.44°，冬至约 −23.44: δ changes with the date: about 0° at the equinoxes, about +23.44° at the June solstice and about -23.44° at the December solstice. You can approximate it with δ ≈ -23.44°*cos(2*pi*(N+10)/365) (N is the day of the year), or use standard astronomical values. Planning commonly uses the Great Cold day (around 20 January) as the minimum sunlight standard.

map.住宅小区规划中，保证后排底层住户在大寒日/冬至日获得规定时长日照，需按太阳高度角: In housing layout planning, to guarantee that the ground-floor residents at the back get the required sunlight duration on the Great Cold day / December solstice, work back from the solar altitude angle to get the minimum building spacing D = H / tan(edge height angle).

map.单栋建筑正午阴影长度 = H / tan(正午太阳高度角)，用于判断对相邻场地的: Noon shadow length of a single building = H / tan(noon solar altitude angle), used to judge how far it shades the neighbouring site.
map.基于太阳高度角与方位角计算保证目标日照时长的最小建筑间距，并给出逐时阴影长度: Computes the minimum building spacing that guarantees the target sunlight duration from the solar altitude and azimuth angles, and gives the hourly shadow length

map.日照间距计算 使用指南: How to use the sunlight spacing calculator
map.简单的 D=H/tan(高度角) 假设遮挡物在正南。实际阴影有东西偏移，北向投影: The simple D=H/tan(altitude angle) assumes the obstruction lies due south. Real shadows shift east and west, and only the northward projection H*cos(azimuth)/tan(altitude angle) is the distance cast in the due north direction, which judges the shading of the plot to the north more accurately.
map.给定目标日照时长 T，取正午前后各 T/2 小时的边缘时刻高度角，得到最不利间距: Given a target sunlight duration T, take the altitude angles at the edge moments T/2 hour before and after noon to get the worst-case spacing, then apply a northward projection correction using the azimuth.
map.：北纬 30°、建筑高 H=30 m、目标日照 T=2 h、日期取冬至（太阳赤纬:
: latitude 30 degN, building height H=30 m, target sunlight T=2 h, date at the December solstice (declination δ≈-23.44 deg):
noon solar altitude = 36.56 deg; altitude at the edge moments (±1 h, hour angle 15 deg) = 34.66 deg.
Minimum sunlight spacing D = 30 / tan(34.66 deg) = 30 / 0.692 ≈ 43.40 m, giving a sunlight spacing coefficient of 1.26.
In other words the front building must stand about 43.4 m or more from the rear one to guarantee one hour of sunlight on each side of noon (2 hours in total) on the December solstice.
